reason: The owner wants the tasks a swamp extension could do found and logged in Capture, not a list of every open task: v1 on the TechWork vault listed 419 tasks, nearly all personal to-dos.

content.problemStatement: Manually reviewing an Obsidian vault to spot tasks or recurring frustrations that could be turned into puddle requests is slow and easy to miss. A list of every open task does not help: on the owner's main vault it is over 400 lines, nearly all personal to-dos, and the few tasks a swamp extension could do are buried in it.
content.desiredOutcome: Once a week, the open tasks in an Obsidian vault that a swamp extension could do are picked out, checked against the extensions that already exist, and each new one is logged in Capture as a draft request with the file and line it came from.

in: Reading the open task lines ("- [ ]") in the vault's Markdown notes, optionally limited to one subfolder
Leaving out templates and daily notes, which repeat the same routine tasks

Deciding for each task, using a model and with a confidence, whether it is worth a reusable swamp extension, a one-off job software could do, or needs a person; the model sees the task with its note and nearest heading
Searching the swamp extension registry for an extension that already covers each candidate
Creating one draft request in Capture for each candidate no extension covers
Running on a weekly schedule, and on demand
out: Proposing, agreeing or building the requests it creates
Merging similar tasks into one request
Tasks that are already done or in progress

constraints: The vault is only read, never written
A task is logged in Capture at most once, across all runs, keyed on its file path and text
The model API key comes from a swamp vault, never from the repo
A task that looks like it holds a secret is not sent to the model or to Capture
Capture is reached only through the methods of the @puddleworks/capture extension, never by writing its data directly
assumptions: Capture is the @puddleworks/capture swamp extension, in the same swamp repo as this workflow; its create_request takes an idempotency key, so a retry never makes a second request
The classifier is Jev through @swamp/typesafe-ai, as puddlerouter uses
Templates live in the vault's Templates folder and daily notes are named YYYY-MM-DD.md

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every open task outside templates and daily notes is classified as worth an extension, a one-off job or needing a person, with the model's confidence; a task is a candidate when the model says it is worth an extension with at least the configured confidence (default 0.5).
A candidate that an existing registry extension covers is reported with that extension's name and is not logged in Capture.
Each other candidate becomes one draft request in Capture, titled from the task, with the vault-relative file path, line and task text in its description.
Running again with no vault changes creates nothing new in Capture.
The vault's files are unchanged after a run.
Each run stores a result listing every task scanned with its classification, confidence, and whether it was logged (with the Capture request link), matched to an extension, skipped, or failed.
If Capture or the model cannot be reached, the run says so and logs nothing it is unsure of; the tasks it missed are picked up by the next run.
